parsed_review.motivation: The documentation change adds guidance on how to propagate transport-specific metadata (such as authentication tokens) to MCP tools, addressing the need for contextual information within an otherwise transport-agnostic framework.
parsed_review.good_points:
Clear explanation of the rationale behind maintaining a transport-agnostic design.
Well-structured AsciiDoc formatting that adheres to the existing project style guide.
Provides a practical, copy-pasteable example of using TransportContextExtractor.
Correct identification of the relevant API components (McpTransportContext, McpSyncRequestContext).
parsed_review.bad_points:
The code example lacks defensive programming practices such as null checks or type safety when interacting with the transport context.
The documentation does not provide a security warning regarding the handling of sensitive headers like 'Authorization'.
Direct casting of context values is prone to runtime errors.
parsed_review.suggestion: Update the documentation example to include null safety checks and explicit warnings about the risks of logging sensitive headers like Authorization. Recommend using defensive coding (e.g., Optional or null checks) when retrieving values from the McpTransportContext.
parsed_review.implementation_details: spring-ai-docs/src/main/antora/modules/ROOT/pages/api/mcp/mcp-server-boot-starter-docs.adoc: Introduces a new section 'Adding data to McpTransportContext'. Demonstrates use of TransportContextExtractor for WebMvcStreamableServerTransportProvider. Illustrates consumption of context data within an @McpTool via McpSyncRequestContext.

issues.title: Missing Null-Safety and Type-Safety in Context Retrieval
issues.detail: The example code retrieves a value from the context using context.get("authorization") and performs an unsafe cast to String. This can lead to NullPointerException or ClassCastException if the key is missing or the object is not a string.

issues.title: Absence of Security Best Practice Warning
issues.detail: The example uses an 'Authorization' header for demonstration. Documentation should explicitly warn developers against logging or exposing these values, as they are security-sensitive.

interpretation_references: This PR adds documentation on how to propagate and access HTTP headers in MCP Servers.
The documentation addresses the discussion in #5374.
The guide explains how to configure a TransportContextExtractor to populate the McpTransportContext.
Populating the McpTransportContext is essential for use cases such as passing Authorization tokens to MCP tools.
interpretation_candidates: Added a new section to the MCP Server Boot Starter documentation titled 'Adding data to McpTransportContext', which provides code examples for configuring a 'TransportContextExtractor' and accessing metadata within tool methods using 'McpSyncRequestContext'.
The original documentation did not explain how to access transport-specific metadata (such as HTTP headers) within tools.

Because the MCP server is designed to be transport-agnostic, providing this guide allows developers to integrate context-sensitive data, like authentication tokens, while maintaining the intended architecture.
